_what: Real main-thread `Stop` hook payloads, captured 2026-09-27 on Claude Code v2.1.283 (headless `-p`, macOS) with a temporary `Stop` command hook (passed via `--settings`) that recorded stdin and printed `{}`. Values sanitized (paths, session/prompt/task ids). This is the evidence behind `validate-code-review-result.py --main-session`: identity comes from the payload's TOP-LEVEL `agent_type`, and `background_tasks[]` must never be read as identity.
_how_to_reproduce: Probe A: pipe a prompt to `-p --settings <hook-settings> --plugin-dir loomwright` telling the main thread to launch ONE `loomwright:code-reviewer` subagent with `run_in_background: true` and end its turn at once. Probe B: same settings plus `--agent loomwright:code-reviewer`, telling it to reply one line and stop. Read the recorded payloads.

observations: No top-level `agent_type` on a plain main thread.

The running reviewer appears ONLY inside `background_tasks[]`, with the plugin-doubled `agent_type`, `type: subagent` and `status: running` — the exact fields the retired prompt hook quoted when it blocked main-thread turn ends ("background_tasks array confirms status is running").

In this single capture the retired prompt hook did not block the first turn end; its verdict on this shape is a model judgement, not a rule (the 2026-09-27 /automate run saw it block every turn end). The command validator allows it deterministically.
An `--agent loomwright:code-reviewer` session carries top-level `agent_type: "loomwright:loomwright:code-reviewer"` (plugin-doubled prefix, as on SubagentStop).

The reply carried no CODE_REVIEW_RESULT block, so the retired prompt hook blocked, correctly for this case: 9 Stop firings, all 9 blocked (9 `Stop hook feedback` messages), the last 8 with `stop_hook_active: true`; the session ended at the runtime's continuation cap. This is the one case the Stop hook exists for, and `--main-session` keeps it covered.
